mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization (depending on country of issuance)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against UN, HM Treasury, OFAC, EU consolidated financial sanctions and the Bermuda consolidated sanctions list. Adherence to BMA AML/CFT Guidance: enhanced due diligence (EDD) for politically exposed persons (PEPs), wire-transfer provenance checks, and source-of-funds verification for any individual or entity holding 25% or more of the partnership. Sanctions screening is performed at pre-incorporation, on an ongoing daily basis, and before any escrow or SWIFT payment.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Bermuda Registrar of Companies e-Registry portal (Bermuda Registry General, Government of Bermuda)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All filings and registered names must be submitted in English; names may use Latin script only; no diacritical marks or non-English characters are accepted; an English transliteration of a foreign commercial name is required for filing.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name refusal carries a written statement of reasons. Applicant may file an administrative appeal within 14 days of notice, supported by legal submissions and a proposed alternative rendered name; if the Registrar remains opposed, the applicant may apply to the Supreme Court of Bermuda for judicial review.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not sufficient to establish the registered office required by the Exempted Limited Partnerships Act 2015. The registered office must be a physical address in Bermuda equipped to accept service of process. Virtual workspace arrangements may support auxiliary administrative functions but cannot satisfy the full registered-office and economic substance physical-presence test under the Economic Substance Act 2018.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate for an aircraft-parts distribution entity engaged in pervasive physical trading and documentation; best estimate 15%-20% likelihood of an unannounced inspection in the first three years, particularly if the economic substance return flags revenue from physical goods.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Exempted Limited Partnerships Act 2015, sections 4–8 (registration, name, registered office, resident agent), read with the Limited Partnerships Act 1883 to the extent not inconsistent.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, Bermuda Registry, Ministry of Finance, Government of Bermuda.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Registration of an Exempted Limited Partnership (Form ELP-1) filed with the Registrar under section 5(1) of the Exempted Limited Partnerships Act 2015.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital. The exempted limited partnership may be registered with zero capital contribution and no escrow bank account deposit is required by Bermuda law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS OF THE GENERAL PARTNER IN LIEU OF A FIRST BOARD MEETING. Whereas the exempted limited partnership is formed for the permitted purpose of surplus commercial aircraft and avionics parts distribution: IT IS RESOLVED that (1) the initial subscription agreements of the limited partners are accepted, and the registered capital is declared as stated in the registration declaration; (2) the registered office of the partnership in Bermuda shall be at the office of the resident agent; (3) the resident agent and the partnership's authorised officer are appointed with authority to open bank accounts and execute all regulatory and licensing filings; and (4) all formation fees, registry filings and exemptions are approved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Bermuda licensed resident agent (corporate services provider) regulated by the Registrar of Companies.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appoint a Bermuda-resident agent licensed under the Companies Act 1981. Provide KYC and beneficial ownership information for the general partner and all limited partners; instruct the agent to prepare the registration declaration and act as the registered office contact.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the resident agent declines to act, select another licensed agent and re-submit the KYC pack within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation application to the Registry. Ensure the proposed name ends with 'Limited Partnership' or 'LP' and is not deceptively similar to an existing Bermuda entity. The resident agent files the application online or by hard copy.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file an amended name reservation within five business days and provide an explanation of any similarity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Bermuda Registry, Ministry of Finance.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form ELP-1 with the Registry, accompanied by the declaration of the general partner and the resident agent consent. Pay the official government fee by domestic wire or cheque through the Bermuda Treasury. The registered office address and general partner details must be stated.
required_dossiers: General partner certificate of good standing (if corporate)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a requisition, respond in writing within 14 calendar days with curative amendments or additional evidence; any administrative cancellation may be cured by re-filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After verification of the declaration, the Registry issues the Certificate of Registration and formally enters the exempted limited partnership on the Bermuda corporate register. Collect the certificate and obtain a certified copy for bank and licensing purposes.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is not issued within the service standard, escalate to the Registrar's senior officer with a written request for expedited issuance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirmation of Registered Office and Officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Bermuda Registry, and Bermuda Ministry of Finance for partnership tax registration record.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the registered office location and resident agent appointment in the public register. File any post-formation notice of general partner or authorised officer details, and obtain a registered office certificate for inclusion in the corporate book.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry record contains mismatched details, submit a supplemental declaration correcting the data and request a reissuance of the certificate.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Bermuda Civil Aviation Authority (BCAA), Aviation Safety and Airworthiness Division.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviation Surplus Parts Distribution Authorisation under the Civil Aviation (Airworthiness) Regulations.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR), Ministry of Environment and Natural Resources, Bermuda.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration-tier only; no full Environmental Impact Assessment required for warehousing and distribution of surplus aircraft parts.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or volatile organic compound sources are anticipated. Handling and storage of aviation fluids or hazardous materials must comply with Bermuda Waste Regulations and spill containment standards; stormwater discharge must remain nil.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Certificate of Fire Safety from the Bermuda Fire and Rescue Service, structural load certification for racking and storage areas, and workplace safety clearance from the Bermuda Department of Occupational Health and Safety.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Office of the Tax Commissioner, Ministry of Finance, Government of Bermuda (portal: www.gov.bm; e-filing via the Bermuda Business Portal); Bermuda Customs and Revenue Department (BCRD) administers customs through ASYCUDA World; Registrar of Companies issues ELP registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Register the ELP with the Registrar of Companies under the Exempted Partnerships Act 1992 via the Bermuda Business Portal and obtain the Certificate of Limited Partnership. 2) Apply to the Office of the Tax Commissioner for a Bermuda TIN (required for payroll tax, customs, social insurance, and bank account opening); issuance typically 5–10 business days. 3) Register with BCRD in ASYCUDA World to obtain an importer/exporter code. 4) If the ELP is owned by non-residents, apply to the Bermuda Monetary Authority (BMA) for non-resident designation and exchange control permission. No minimum capital and no notarization required; the entire process is electronic.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible. Bermuda imposes no income, capital gains, or withholding tax on ELPs or their non-resident partners; the ELP is fiscally transparent by default, and each partner is taxed in its own residence jurisdiction. For UK purposes the ELP is a transparent partnership unless the UK hybrid mismatch rules (TIOPA 2010 Part 6A) recharacterise it. The Bermuda Corporate Income Tax Act 2024 (15% for in-scope MNE groups with EUR 750M+ consolidated revenue) does not alter the pass-through default for a stand-alone ELP.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: 1) Election for separate legal personality under s.5A Exempted Partnerships Act 1992 (inserted 2015); if not elected, the ELP remains a contractual partnership. 2) Tax assurance certificate under the Exempted Undertakings Tax Protection Act 1966, guaranteeing exemption from any future Bermuda income, capital, or withholding tax for 50 years (protection extended to 2050 by the 2021 amendment). 3) No Bermuda check-the-box election exists; US partners may file IRS Form 8832 to affirm or override US entity classification, and UK partners may file election alignments under TIOPA 2010 Part 6A where an entity is transparent in Bermuda but opaque in the UK.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No VAT, GST, or sales-and-use tax in Bermuda. Indirect taxation comprises Customs Duties (Customs Tariff Act 1989), Stamp Duties (Stamps Act 1976), and Payroll Tax (Payroll Tax Act 1995). The UK VAT regime has no territorial application to Bermuda, and the UK 20% VAT is not chargeable on Bermuda transactions.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable — Bermuda has no VAT registration threshold. Every employer with Bermuda payroll must register for payroll tax from the first BMD of remuneration (small business relief applies). Every importer must obtain a BCRD customs code in ASYCUDA World for each import; no de minimis turnover exemption applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, CTC/CIUS, or mandatory e-invoicing regime exists in Bermuda. Customs entries are filed electronically through ASYCUDA World; payroll tax and social insurance returns are e-filed via the Bermuda Business Portal. Statutory invoices follow common-law commercial form with no digital stamping or government clearance requirement.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable as a VAT concept because Bermuda has no VAT. For customs duty purposes: goods exported from Bermuda are duty-free, and surplus commercial aircraft rotables/avionics imported for re-export may be entered duty-free under the in-transit, transshipment, and temporary admission regimes of the Customs Act 1989 and Customs Tariff Act 1989, subject to a duty deposit or approved bonded warehouse and a documented re-export undertaking. A refund of customs duty may be claimed if duty was paid and the goods are subsequently exported within the approved period (generally 12 months). Non-resident ELPs obtain BMA permission to maintain offshore foreign-currency accounts; the default 180-day export-proceeds repatriation rule applies only to Bermuda-resident traders.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bermuda Customs Export Declaration (ASYCUDA World electronic entry)
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill (original or certified electronic)
Commercial Invoice and Packing List with ISIC 4659 / HS 8803 avionic part descriptions
Re-Export Undertaking / Temporary Admission Certificate or Customs Bond
Inward Remittance Certificate (where duty drawback or deposit refund is claimed)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent export zero-rating claims cannot arise in the absence of VAT, but false customs declarations and re-export fraud attract: forfeiture of goods; fines up to BMD 10,000 per offence under the Customs Act 1989, plus a merchantable-value penalty of up to BMD 30,000 per unit; imprisonment up to 5 years for fraudulent duty evasion; and additional penalties of up to 200% of the unpaid duty. Any duty refund or deposit is clawed back if the goods are not exported within the approved period or the re-export undertaking is breached. The BMA may impose exchange-control sanctions and the Registrar of Companies may strike off the ELP; for UK-resident partners, false relief claims trigger HMRC penalties under FA 2007 Sch. 24 together with retrospective closure and assessment for unpaid UK duty or VAT.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bermuda Monetary Authority (BMA), exercising delegated powers under the Bermuda Monetary Authority Act 1969 and the Exchange Control Act 1972.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Bermuda dollar (BMD) is pegged 1:1 to the United States dollar (USD). For an Exempted Limited Partnership (ELP) classified as non-resident for exchange control purposes, capital account convertibility is substantially liberalized: non-resident contributions may be received in USD or convertible foreign currency into approved Foreign Currency Accounts, and external remittance of trading profits and capital is generally permitted without prior BMA approval. Current account payments for genuine commercial transactions are also freely remittable, subject to standard AML/KYC verification. The key residual hurdle is that any transaction settling in BMD with a Bermuda-resident counterparty, or any conversion from BMD into another currency outside an authorized dealer relationship, may require BMA exchange control consent. For this aircraft-parts distribution ELP, maintaining USD-denominated accounts and invoicing in USD avoids the main convertibility friction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Section 3 of the Exchange Control Act 1972 imposes an obligation on Bermuda residents to offer export proceeds in foreign currency to an authorized dealer within a statutory timeline, typically three months from receipt, unless a general or specific exemption is granted. A non-resident Exempted Limited Partnership is normally granted an exemption from surrender for USD proceeds received from the export of certified civil aircraft rotables and avionics surplus, provided the proceeds are held in an approved Foreign Currency Account maintained with a BMA-licensed authorized dealer. The partnership must evidence this exemption in its bank account file, record the relevant BMA authorization reference, and ensure that no portion of export proceeds is converted into BMD without prior BMA or authorized-dealer consent.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: The Bank of N.T. Butterfield & Son Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Foreign Currency USD Account
Operational USD Account / Settlement Account for Trade Finance

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-Low. Bermuda does not operate a domestic e-money institution (EMI) licensing regime equivalent to the United Kingdom's Financial Conduct Authority EMI authorization. Offshore digital EMIs cannot join Bermuda's local clearing and settlement system, cannot hold BMD settlement balances with BMA directly, and are not recognized as authorized dealers under the Exchange Control Act. Such EMIs may be used solely as a complementary collection/distribution or card-acquiring rail where the ultimate settlement account sits with a BMA-regulated licensed bank. A UK or European EMI must therefore be treated as a non-bank payment intermediary, not as the primary treasury clearing bank, and the ELP must maintain legal ownership over funds in the underlying licensed bank account to avoid money-flow opacity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Bermuda law does not impose a blanket statutory requirement for all directors or partners to appear physically before a bank. In practice, BMA-regulated banks require a face-to-face interview for the beneficial owners or the general partner's senior management unless the ELP is introduced by a recognized professional introducer such as a Bermuda law firm, licensed corporate service provider, or auditor. Remote opening is viable for a non-resident ELP if the introduction letter confirms the identity of the general partner and underlying limited partners, the entity has a current certificate of compliance and LEI, and the bank completes an enhanced video interview. Some banks will still require one authorized signatory to attend physically in Bermuda or at a correspondent branch in Hong Kong/Singapore/London for high-risk jurisdictions. The general partner should therefore budget for a minimum of one physical or notarized overseas interview and a possible Bermuda board meeting.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex intermediate ownership chain involving the Bermuda ELP, multiple offshore intermediate holding companies, and nominee limited partners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete corporate chart showing each layer from ultimate beneficial owner to the ELP; certified copies of certificate of limited partnership, certificate of compliance, limited partnership agreement, and registered agent's letter of good standing; register of beneficial ownership filed under the Economic Substance and Beneficial Ownership framework; signed indemnity and consent letters for each intermediate holding vehicle; and an organization chart endorsed by the Bermuda corporate service provider.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds opacity for large capital contributions used to purchase surplus commercial aircraft parts inventory.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements or management accounts of the contributing partner; bank references from the source bank; three months of bank statements evidencing accumulation of funds; sale and purchase contracts for prior aviation parts transactions; customs declarations; and an independent accountant's source-of-wealth report where contribution exceeds USD 1 million.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and dual-use / export-control risk associated with civil aircraft parts, especially when counterparties or end-users are located in a high-risk jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A written sanctions and export-control compliance policy; end-user certificates and non-incorporation of military-use aviation parts; manufacturer's Certificates of Airworthiness and traceability documents; harmonized commodity code and ECCN classification; a current denied-party screening report from a reputable screening provider; and a transaction-by-transaction explainer showing that all parts are unambiguously commercial civil surplus.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP or politically exposed person status of any limited partner, officer, or general partner representative.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A documented PEP register; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence; proof of employment or business ownership for the period preceding the capital injection; a reputable independent PEP-screening output; and a formal risk memorandum prepared by the compliance adviser explaining the rationale for the commercial relationship and the AML controls applied.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections should flow by SWIFT MT103 from the contributing limited partner's or general partner's overseas bank account to the Bermuda ELP's USD Foreign Currency Account at Butterfield, HSBC Bermuda, or Clarien Bank. The beneficiary field must name the ELP exactly as registered, followed by its Bermuda registration number and LEI. The payment details field should state 'Capital Contribution — Exempted Limited Partnership' and reference the registered limited partnership agreement. For amounts above USD 100,000, the remitter must supply a source-of-funds memorandum, bank reference, and inbound remittance declaration. If funds originate in a non-convertible currency or a BMD-denominated domestic wire is used, the BMA exchange control exemption reference should be quoted. All inbound wires must be pre-notified to the relationship manager to prevent an automatic AML hold.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade disbursements should use SWIFT MT103 for open-account or cash-against-documents payments to suppliers and MRO facilities, and commercial letters of credit (MT700 / MT710) or documentary collections (MT740) for higher-value aircraft parts purchases where title documents, certificates of airworthiness, and shipping documents must be exchanged. The bank's trade finance desk may establish a revolving import/export LC facility secured against trade receivables. For escrow-backed aviation transactions, the operational account should be paired with an escrow sub-account at The Bank of N.T. Butterfield & Son Limited under an escrow agreement naming the seller and buyer. The outbound routing must include references to the underlying invoice number, commercial contract, and Incoterms rule, and must align with the BMA-authorized dealer's reporting thresholds.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright foreign exchange forwards with a BMA-licensed authorized dealer, limited to the currency of genuine aviation trade exposure (USD, EUR, GBP, CAD).
Cross-currency swaps for EUR/USD and GBP/USD cash-flow exposures arising from the purchase or sale of surplus aircraft parts.
Synthetic forward structures created through a matched deposit and borrowing pair, provided both legs are settled with the same BMA-licensed counterparty.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for exotic or restricted-market currencies only, subject to BMA exchange control and bank internal policy approval; NDFs are not necessary for BMD because of the 1:1 USD peg.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, Government of Bermuda
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary-based; filing due on or before each annual anniversary of registration, with a 60-day grace period allowed by the Registrar for certain non-resident partnerships
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of BMD 100 per month up to a maximum BMD 500; continued delinquency may trigger an administrative strike-off and forfeiture of the entity's name after 6 months of non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies (Beneficial Ownership Filing Portal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary-based; due in parallel with the Exempted Partnership Annual Return (within 30 days of the entity's compliance date)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Initial penalty BMD 250, increasing to BMD 500 for persistent default; administrative strike-off may be initiated after 3 months of non-filing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies (Economic Substance Online System)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the end of the ELP's financial year (default financial year is 31 December)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file may attract a daily penalty of BMD 100; the Registry may also issue a direction requiring production of accounts; substantial non-compliance may expose the entity to fines up to BMD 250,000

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary-based; submission is required at the time of the annual return if the general partner is not ordinarily resident in Bermuda
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain a Bermuda resident representative is a continuing offence under the Exempted Partnerships Act 1992 and may result in a default fine of BMD 10 per day plus potential strike-off

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No universal statutory audit requirement applies to a Bermuda Exempted Limited Partnership. A mandatory independent audit is triggered only if the ELP: (i) is a regulated entity under the Insurance Act 1978, the Investment Funds Act 2006, or similar; (ii) elects to file consolidated financial statements under the Economic Substance (Bermuda) Amendment Act 2018 for a distribution and service center activity; or (iii) its constitutive Limited Partnership Agreement contains a mandatory audit provision.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Bermuda Financial Reporting Standards (converged with IFRS) or IFRS as issued by the IASB; in the absence of a statutory imposition, the accounting framework shall be that stipulated in the Limited Partnership Agreement.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Companies and Limited Liability Company (Beneficial Ownership) Amendment Regulations 2018 and the Beneficial Ownership Act 2017, the ELP must maintain a Beneficial Ownership Register identifying any individual partner who directly or indirectly holds 25% or more of partnership interests or control. An annual confirmation of the UBO register is filed with the Registrar on the compliance date; any change in beneficial ownership during the year must be reported within 30 days of the change.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of the General Partner (as applicable)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% — Bermuda Corporate Income Tax (CIT) Act 2023, effective for income years beginning on or after 1 January 2025; the 15% rate applies to the ascertainable net income / GloBE income of taxable Bermuda entities, including in-scope exempted limited partnerships (ELPs) that are constituent entities of multinational enterprise (MNE) groups with consolidated annual revenue of EUR 750 million or more in at least two of the four preceding years.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Bermuda has no general corporate income tax outside the Pillar Two charge and grants no statutory tax holidays. Incentives that lower the effective burden for in-scope groups include: (i) the Substance-Based Income Exclusion (SBIE) on qualified payroll (10% phasing down to 5% by 2033) and qualified tangible assets (8% phasing down to 5%); (ii) the Bermuda Domestic Minimum Top-Up Tax (DMTT) which discharges GloBE top-up tax liability under the IIR/UTPR rules; (iii) Qualified Refundable Tax Credit offsets; (iv) transitional simplification and de-minimis safe harbour reliefs in the first reporting years; and (v) for out-of-scope standalone domestic groups and fiscally transparent ELPs, an effective rate of nil.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Bermuda Corporate Income Tax Return (Form CIT-1) and, for in-scope MNE members, the supplementary GloBE Information Return (GIR) and CbCR-safe-harbour certification, all filed through the Bermuda Tax Administration Portal (TAP) operated by the Office of the Tax Commissioner (OTC) at taxt.gov.bm.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly estimated top-up tax instalments are payable on the 15th day of the 4th, 7th, 10th and 13th months after the start of the fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual CIT-1 return is due no later than 15 months after the end of the fiscal year for the first two years of the regime and no later than 12 months after the fiscal year-end thereafter; the GIR follows the same 15-month/12-month deadlines and is exchanged automatically with HMRC and other tax administrations under the OECD Multilateral Competent Authority Agreement on GloBE Information Returns.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part I, Box 1a — BTR and Legal Name
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Bermuda Tax Reference (BTR) number and the exact registered legal name of the ELP or the constituent entity filing the return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the BTR allocated by the OTC at registration; do not duplicate partner-level returns; the general partner signs under penalty of perjury even when all limited partners are non-resident.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selection of the applicable status: (A) in-scope MNE member subject to CIT; (B) domestic top-up tax group member; (C) out-of-scope entity seeking confirmation of non-liability; (D) transitional relief claimant.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For the aviation spares wholesale ELP, category A applies if the UK ultimate parent group exceeds the EUR 750 million consolidated revenue threshold in the preceding four-year look-back; mark category B where the Bermuda DMTT election is made.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part II, Line 2 — Accounting Period and Currency
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Start and end dates of the fiscal year stated to the day, and the reporting currency (BMD).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Align the filing period with the consolidated accounting period of the UK ultimate parent entity; for a pass-through ELP the entity-level period remains the partnership tax year and each partner's distributable share must be recorded as a schedule attachment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part II, Line 3 — Ultimate Parent Entity Identifier
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name, jurisdiction of tax residence, and tax identification number (TIN) of the ultimate parent entity, expected to be a UK registered company with an HMRC UTR.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Standard link to the GIR and CbCR; failure to disclose the UK parent correctly exposes the group to information-sharing penalties in the United Kingdom under the GloBE implementation rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part III, Line 4 — GloBE Income (Loss) Before Elections
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of GloBE income or loss before elections, using the consolidated financial reporting base with GloBE adjustments, covering the wholesale distribution margin on surplus commercial aircraft rotables and avionics.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Commissions, intercompany purchases and storage fees payable to the UK parent must satisfy arm's length pricing; attach Form CIT-TP transfer pricing schedules; distributions to partners are not deductible in computing GloBE income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part III, Line 5 — Covered Taxes and Effective Tax Rate
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate covered taxes (Bermuda CIT and any foreign covered taxes attributed to the Bermuda entity) and computation of the jurisdictional effective tax rate (ETR).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners should verify that foreign withholding on their share of profits is not double-counted at both entity and partner levels; reconciliation to the partnership agreement and GIR is mandatory.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part IV, Line 6 — Substance-Based Income Exclusion
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculation of the SBIE based on qualifying Bermuda payroll costs and qualifying tangible assets used in the surplus parts distribution activity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Assets physically located in third-country warehouses of the UK parent cannot be claimed; to preserve the SBIE and economic substance, the ELP must maintain real Bermudian premises, staff and bookkeeping records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part V, Line 7 — Top-Up Tax and Bermuda DMTT
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of top-up tax after ETR, application of the Bermuda domestic minimum top-up tax discharge, payment of any balance due, and interest on deferred instalments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The ELP must appoint a tax representative resident in Bermuda; non-resident partners who close the entity before finalisation risk a personal assessment and lien on distributions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file on time: fixed penalty of BMD 10,000 plus BMD 100 per day of continued default (capped at BMD 100,000). Negligent inaccuracies: penalty up to BMD 50,000. Deliberate understatement: additional tax not exceeding double the understated top-up tax plus interest at 8% per annum from the due date. Criminal prosecution under s. 66 of the CIT Act 2023 may result on conviction in fines and imprisonment up to 10 years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Partnership Information Return (PIR) and the Economic Substance Act 2018 (ESA) Annual Return, filed through the Bermuda Registrar of Companies COMPAS e-filing portal, supplemented by the s. 137 Companies Act 1981 Statement of Partners.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, aligned to the partnership fiscal year; changes to the register of partners must be notified within 30 days.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The PIR and the ESA Annual Return must be filed no later than six months after the end of the partnership's accounting period; the initial statement on formation of the ELP is due within 30 days of registration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box A — General Partner and Resident Agent
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, Bermuda registration number and registered office address of the general partner, together with the name of any Bermudian resident agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The general partner must be a Bermuda exempted company; a non-resident limited partner may not serve as general partner in a compliant Bermuda ELP.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box B — Schedule of Limited Partners
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full name, country of tax residence, TIN, capital contribution and profit share percentage of each limited partner.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: UK-resident limited partners must provide HMRC UTRs; the schedule is exchanged under the OECD CRS and the UK/Bermuda exchange of information channels; a missing resident partner disclosure invokes CFC scrutiny.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selection of the relevant activity; for ISIC 4659 wholesale distribution of certified aircraft rotables and avionics, the correct class is 'Distribution and Service Centre'.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A pure letterbox classification is fatal; describe the actual trade flow of surplus aircraft parts from procurement to sale as distribution activity carried on in Bermuda.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box D — Gross Income and CIGA Description
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income and gross operating expenses of the distribution activity together with a narrative of core income-generating activities (order taking, transport and storage, invoicing, credit management and stock control).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The margin reported must reconcile with Form CIT-1, Line 4; intercompany purchase prices must be supported by the CUP benchmark or TNMM/Berry Ratio documentation for the parts traded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Number of full-time employees in Bermuda, floor area of premises occupied, annual operating expenditure incurred in Bermuda, and number of partner or director meetings held in Bermuda.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Adequacy is proportionate to the volume and value of aircraft parts turnover; the ELP cannot rely exclusively on UK parent employees or shared services without a Bermuda cost allocation and service agreement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box F — Declaration and Government Fee
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Certification by the general partner that the information is true and complete, together with acknowledgement of the annual exempted partnership government fee.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The declaration is made under the Companies Act 1981 and the ESA 2018; making a false declaration exposes the signing general partner to personal penalties and disqualification.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the PIR: automatic penalty of BMD 500 per month or part thereof, capped at BMD 6,000, and a fine on summary conviction of up to BMD 10,000. ESA non-compliance: a penalty of up to BMD 120,000 for failing the economic substance test, a further BMD 5,000 per month for continuing lack of substance, and ultimately strike-off and cancellation of the ELP's exempted status by the Registrar.
